newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower as market readies for CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower as market readies for CPI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed weaker on Monday as banks took positions ahead of Friday's December quarter inflation data.
The currency finished at US$0.7042/49 and 67.92 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.7062/69 and 68.31 at the open.
Dealers said there had been strong selling from a local institution, apparently on expectations that inflation would be low enough to allow further falls in interest rates.

"I guess also there's a possibility at the end of the week the Reserve Bank may say something about the mix of currency and rates so people may be a little nervous about that," an Auckland trader said.
Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash has consistently said he would prefer a lower currency and higher rates if the bank could directly control the mix of monetary conditions.

Economists in a Reuter survey forecast on average a 0.4 percent quarterly rate of underlying inflation, for an annual 2.15 percent. They said any number in line with or lower than the Reserve Bank's forecasts of 0.5 percent and 2.3 percent
would trigger a fall in interest rates.
Dealers said there was good two-way business and the range of 0.7046-78 was the widest for some time.
"At the moment the range to me would appear to be 0.7020-70, perhaps with a slight bias down towards Friday," a Wellington dealer said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
